biggest_catch: $0 annual fee the first year, then $99 — do the fee math: the 50,000 miles are only valuable if you actually fly Frontier, and year two costs $99 whether you use the card or not. If you will not fly Frontier, you paid $99 for miles gathering dust. Only net purchases count toward the $1,000-in-90-days, so spend only what you already planned — never buy extra to hit it. Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, and carrying a balance at the card's ~20%+ variable APR erases the miles fast — pay in full every month.
catches: Only pursue spending you already planned to do — never buy extra things just to hit a bonus threshold; overspending to chase a bonus wipes out the bonus math and is how people lose money on it.
The miles are Frontier miles — worthless if you do not fly Frontier; do not chase them for cash value.
The $99 annual fee starts in year two; set a reminder to cancel or reassess before it hits if the card does not earn its keep.
Only net purchases count toward the $1,000; returns and cash-like transactions do not.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily dip your credit score by a few points.
The card's variable APR (~20%+) will erase the miles' value fast if you carry a balance — pay the full statement balance every month.

steps: Go to the official Barclays Frontier terms and read the 50,000-mile / $1,000 / 90-day terms and the $99 year-two fee.
Apply online and get approved; save your approval confirmation.
Spend $1,000 in net purchases — your already-planned spending — within the first 90 days.
Pay the full statement balance every month so interest never eats the bonus.
Allow 4–6 weeks after you qualify, then confirm the 50,000 FRONTIER Miles posted.
timing: Bonus miles post within 4–6 weeks after qualification.
